new_statements.quote: Ударение слова в целом тяготеет к конечному слогу, однако в формах слов с узким конечным гласным ударение смещается на предыдущий широкий гласный: парча ‘весь; все’; парчаларда ‘во всех; везде’; парчозун ‘(вижу его / их) весь’; парчалорунда ‘во всех (их); везде’.
new_statements.translation: Word stress on the whole gravitates to the final syllable; however, in word forms with a narrow (high) final vowel the stress shifts to the preceding broad (non-high) vowel: parča 'all; everyone'; parčalarda 'in all; everywhere'; parčozun '(I see him/them) all'; parčalorunda 'in all (of them); everywhere'.
new_statements.citation: Kondiyakov, A. F. & V. M. Lemskaya. 2021. Chulymskij jazyk d. Pasechnoe Tjukhtetskogo rajona Krasnojarskogo kraja 2007-2021 gg. Tom I: Slovar', formy slov i grammaticheskie primery. Tomsk: Izdatel'stvo Tomskogo universiteta (sci. ed. A. V. Dybo).

The Tom II copy ( p. 10 = printed p. 8) is the same rule but NOT strictly verbatim: 'к последнему слогу' for 'к конечному слогу' and different gloss punctuation ("парча ‘весь’; ‘все’.. парчозун (вижу его / их) ‘весь’"). The examples are p…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Default final-syllable stress; if the last syllable contains a high ('narrow') vowel, stress retracts to the nearest preceding syllable with a non-high ('broad') vowel. A vowel-quality-sensitive coding (default-final, high vowels skipped) would also be defensible.
new_statements.exceptions: Only the high-final-vowel retraction; the hedge 'в целом' (on the whole) signals a tendency rather than an exceptionless rule. No statement about loanwords or suffix classes.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level; stated for inflected word forms (case/possessive forms) of the Melet subdialect of Middle Chulym as spoken by A. F. Kondiyakov (Pasechnoe, Krasnoyarsk Krai), i.e. not for Lower Chulym proper. Based on field data 2007-2018; the Melet text on the minlang portal marks stress consistently with this rule.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog 5.1 chul1246 = Lower Chulym (Chibi, Ketsik, Küärik, Yezhi, Yatsi), effectively extinct; Middle Chulym (Tutal, Melet/'Ös') is filed under Shor (tuta1234 'Tutal Middle Chulym', shor1247) in Glottolog 5.1, while ISO 639-3 clw and WALS 'Chulym' (Birjukovich 1997) cover all Chulym varieties. The quoted statement describes the Melet subdialect of Middle Chulym (village Pasechnoe, Tyukhtet district, Krasnoyarsk Krai; speaker A. F. Kondiyakov), not Lower Chulym proper; no stress statement for Lower Chulym itself was reachable (Dul'zon 1952/1966, Birjukovich 1979/1997 not online). Pomorska 2001, the source named by the earlier scan, was opened and is silent on stress.

sources.note: p. 23 (Melet subdialect of Middle Chulym): word stress on the whole gravitates to the final syllable; in forms with a narrow (high) final vowel it shifts to the preceding broad vowel (parča, parčalarda vs. parčozun, parčalorunda). sources.citation: Pomorska, Marzanna. 2001. The Chulyms and their language. An attempt at a description of Chulym phonetics and nominal morphology. Türk Dilleri Araştırmaları 11: 75-123.
sources.note: Section 5 Phonology (5.1 Vowels pp. 83-89, 5.2-5.3 Consonants pp. 89-97) treats the 8-vowel system, long vowels, reduced vowels, diphthongs, harmony and consonants of Küerik, Lower and Middle Chulym; it says nothing about stress or accent (a full-text search for stress/accent/Betonung: 0 hits). Its reference list identifies Birjukovich 1979 'Zvukovoj stroj čulymsko-tjurkskogo jazyka' (ZS) as the phonology monograph and Menges 1955 (CAJ 1) as the South-Siberian phonology survey.

Tomskij zhurnal lingvisticheskikh i antropologicheskikh issledovanij (Tomsk Journal of Linguistics and Anthropology) 2025, 3 (49): 29-47. doi:10.23951/2307-6119-2025-3-29-47
sources.note: Describes another variety (Glottolog mele1253). Historical-phonological account of the Middle Chulym vowel system (Proto-Turkic length lost, secondary/compensatory length, diphthongs); states that Middle Chulym stress falls by default on the last syllable and is retracted onto a preceding wide vowel before a narrow/reduced vowel, with compensatory lengthening; the only tone-adjacent remark is that 'the question of the link between primary length and the pharyngealization noted in Chulym at the phonetic level [11, p. 107] remains open'. No statement on tone or contrastive pitch.

sources.citation: Urtegeshev, N. S. 2016. Fonetika chulymsko-tjurkskogo jazyka po zapisjam 70-kh godov XX veka [The phonetics of the Chulym language according to the recordings of the 1970s]. Uralo-altajskie issledovanija (Ural-Altaic Studies) 2016, No. 1 (20): 105-110.
sources.note: Describes another variety (Glottolog mele1253). Experimental-phonetic re-analysis; section 1 'Faringalizacija' reports pharyngealized vowel settings in Chulym for the first time and classifies the pharyngealization 'by type of tone' (pitch contour: falling-rising long, falling short - 'apparently also in Chulym' - and level/compensatory) and by duration, with examples (аът 'horse', сооъқ 'hit!'); section 2 describes 'interrupted' (glottal-stop-split) vowels. It treats these as phonetic settings; it does NOT claim contrastive lexical tone and gives no statement on word stress.

tone.quote: В чулымско-тюркском языке нами были выявлены разные типы фарингализации: по типу тона, по длительности. Все эти типы фарингализаций встречаются в сибирских языках, и не только в тюркских, только одни типы доминируют в одних языках, а другие — в других (ср., например, нисходяще-восходящий долгий в тувинском [Дамбыра 2005; Селютина, Уртегешев и др. 2014] и тубинском [Сарбашева 2004] или нисходяще-краткий в шорском [Уртегешев 2012: 41—43], похоже и в чулымском).
tone.translation: In Chulym Turkic we identified different types of pharyngealization: by type of tone (pitch contour) and by duration. All these types of pharyngealization occur in Siberian languages, and not only Turkic ones; some types dominate in some languages and others in others (cf., e.g., the falling-rising long type in Tuvan [Dambyra 2005; Selyutina, Urtegeshev et al. 2014] and Tuba [Sarbasheva 2004], or the falling short type in Shor [Urtegeshev 2012: 41-43], apparently also in Chulym).
